transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-16
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~60 minutes
Attendees: Ava Martinez (Redwood AE), Leo Chen (Redwood SE), Maya Patel (Redwood CSM); Janelle Rivers (CTO), Marcus Lee (Head of ML), Priya Shah (DevOps), Samir Khan (Security)

[00:00:00] Ava (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for jumping on. quick intro round please, then we'll walk through goals and proposed onboarding plan. sorry if there's any audio hiccups.
[00:00:15] Janelle (CTO): Hi all, Janelle here. excited to get Redwood running; main ask is to get a pilot up and running by end of month, and then a production rollout by quarter end.
[00:00:28] Marcus (Head of ML): Marcus, i lead the models team. we'll be evaluating embeddings + chat flows initially. our main constraints are latency under 200ms for short queries and strict PHI handling.
[00:00:43] Priya (DevOps): Priya, i'll own the infra side. we need details on VPC peering, firewall rules, and any static IPs.
[00:00:50] Samir (Security): Samir, security. SOC2 is required, we also need KMS integration and audit logs retention details.
[00:00:58] Ava: Awesome. quick intros from our side — Leo is our solutions engineer who'll handle the infra and benchmark work, Maya is your CSM who'll manage the project timeline.

[00:01:20] Leo (Redwood SE): Hey everyone. quick note: we'll propose either hosted-api for fast start or dedicated for predictable latency/cost once you scale; private/VPC option is also supported for regulated data. we'll scope requirements today.

[00:02:00] Maya (CSM): I'll map milestones and run the onboarding checklist — admin account, API keys, sample prompts, benchmark plan.

[00:02:25] Janelle: Sounds good. Marcus, do you want to talk about success criteria?
[00:02:32] Marcus: yeah, two primary metrics: 1) avg latency for 1-2 turn chat under 200ms 2) embedding recall/quality on our eval set - we have an internal MRR baseline. also cost: we need to discuss cost per 1k tokens and expected throughput.
[00:03:05] Ava: Great. we typically start hosted to validate quality/queries and then move to dedicated if latency/cost tradeoffs demand it. for PHI, many customers go dedicated or private for data isolation; we can also offer dedicated capacity with customer-managed KMS.
[00:03:40] Samir: Can you share SOC2 and encryption at-rest details? how do audit logs look?
[00:03:47] Leo: quick answer: Redwood has SOC2 Type II, supports customer KMS via our private plane integrations (we-- sorry, private control plane with KMS). audit logs can be exported to your SIEM via S3 or a webhook; retention is configurable. i'll share the security pack.
[00:04:15] Samir: ok, please share. also need data residency options - some workloads must stay in east coast region.
[00:04:25] Ava: noted. we have region selection and can route traffic to specific regions; private deployments allow on-prem if required but that's a longer lead.
[00:05:00] Priya: on networking — do you require peering or is NAT + egress rules enough? we prefer peering for stability.
[00:05:10] Leo: peering is supported for dedicated and private; hosted uses secure egress and TLS with IP allowlist. for peering we'll send a network runbook (VPC CIDRs, ports 443, 80, and any management ports) — i'll put that in the notes.
[00:05:45] Marcus: about model catalog - do we bring our own models or use Redwood-curated open models? we might start with open LLMs and later evaluate fine-tuned privately.
[00:05:55] Ava: you can do both; we'll help onboard open models first for speed, then help with fine-tuning or private model hosting. note that for fine-tuning with PHI we recommend private/dedicated with KMS.
[00:06:30] Janelle: timeline — we want pilot in two weeks if possible. is that realistic?
[00:06:36] Maya: Pilot in two weeks is aggressive but doable if we get sample prompts, eval set, and network contacts within 48 hours. otherwise three weeks is safer.
[00:07:05] Ava: ok i'll list required artifacts: sample prompts & eval suite, list of endpoints and expected QPS, security contacts, and network details.
[00:07:25] Marcus: we'll share eval set and sample payloads by Monday.
[00:07:35] Priya: i'll share network contacts and our peering policy by Tuesday.
[00:07:45] Samir: i'll review the SOC2 docs once you send them. also need details on data deletion and retention for logs.
[00:08:00] Leo: deletion: we can configure retention windows and have options to disable retention for certain flows; for dedicated/private we can ensure no logs persist beyond audit window. i'll include specifics.
[00:08:20] Ava: switching to integration plan - high level: 1) create admin account + org, 2) provision test API keys and sandbox workspace, 3) run initial smoke tests with sample prompts, 4) run benchmark run (latency/cost) and evaluate.
[00:08:48] Leo: for SDKs we have node/python examples, and streaming support if you need partial tokens. batching and prefix caching recommendations will be provided based on your request patterns.
[00:09:10] Marcus: we have heavy reuse of prefixes for embedding retrievals; caching would help. what are typical batching config suggestions?
[00:09:18] Leo: depends on distribution; we'll look at request histograms but a typical starting point is 32-64 batch for embeddings and small batch sizes for chat to keep latency low. Redwood Optimize can suggest configs after initial logs.
[00:09:45] Janelle: about costs — can we get a ballpark for hosted vs dedicated?
[00:09:52] Ava: i'll send a cost sheet; hosted is pay-as-you-go with per-token pricing, dedicated is a commit model with predictable unit economics. for your throughput we can model both once we have QPS and token estimates.
[00:10:20] Samir: legal questions — data processing agreement, subprocessor list. who is the contract owner for Redwood?
[00:10:26] Ava: our legal will send DPA and subprocessor list; i'll be the commercial owner and our contracts team will be the contact.
[00:10:45] Maya: project cadence proposal: weekly 30-min sync for first month, then biweekly; channel in Slack/email for ad-hoc. I'll set up a shared docs folder with milestones.
[00:11:05] Marcus: agreed.
[00:11:20] Leo: technical deep-dive scheduling — i'd like to schedule the infra and benchmark session next week with Priya and Samir. 60-90 minutes to go through VPC, peering, and runbook.
[00:11:35] Priya: next week Tue/Wed morning looks good.
[00:11:45] Ava: we'll pencil in Tuesday 14th? sorry, date mismatch — today is 16th July so next Tuesday is 21st — can we aim for 2026-07-21 14:00 UTC?
[00:11:58] Priya: 21st 14:00 UTC works.
[00:12:10] Samir: want to validate SLA and support channels — production SRE on call?
[00:12:18] Ava: for production we have premium SLA add-on; support tiers and escalation path included; i'll attach support doc.
[00:12:35] Janelle: ok good. any blockers we should call out?
[00:12:40] Marcus: only blocker would be if we can't get peering or KMS integrated quickly; that would push to private/dedicated timelines.
[00:12:55] Leo: noted. we'll prep a fallback plan: start hosted for data that is not PHI and dedicated/private for PHI flows.
[00:13:20] Ava: quick note on benchmarks — we'll run a 24h pilot to capture tail latency and cost. Marcus, can you provide 500-1k sample queries?
[00:13:29] Marcus: yes, we'll prepare 1k with distribution markers.
[00:13:40] Maya: i'll coordinate scheduling and make sure action items are in CRM.
[00:14:00] Ava: recap of next steps: 1) Ava to send onboarding deck + security pack (tomorrow), 2) Leo to send network runbook and schedule infra deep-dive (2026-07-21), 3) Marcus to share eval set (2026-07-20), 4) Priya to provide peering details (2026-07-22), 5) Maya to set up project calendar and weekly syncs.
[00:14:35] Janelle: thanks — that lines up. any questions?
[00:14:40] Samir: one small question — regarding key rotation, how often is that supported?
[00:14:45] Leo: rotation is customer-controlled via KMS; we support automated rotation windows or manual rotation, and we'll document typical practices.
[00:15:05] Marcus: also curious about model version pinning during rollouts to avoid regressions.
[00:15:11] Ava: we support model version pinning and can do canary rollouts with automatic fallback; Redwood Optimize has regression alerts tied to eval prompts.
[00:15:30] Priya: perfect.
[00:15:35] Ava: ok we'll close here — Maya will send the invite for weekly syncs, Leo will send the network runbook and security docs, and I'll send pricing and onboarding deck. thanks everyone.
[00:15:50] Maya: thanks all.
[00:16:00] Janelle: thanks, talk soon.
